newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Banco de Colombia confirms alliance with BCH.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Colombia confirms alliance with BCH.

text.p: Banco de Colombia confirmed Thursday that it had reached an agreement in principle to enter into a "strategic" partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispano (BCH).
Under terms of the agreement, BCH will become a "strategic partner in the development of banking activity in Colombia," Banco de Colombia said in a statement.
It added that the partnership would also lead to "the joint development of banking activities in the northern part of the Latin American continent," but failed to name any specific countries.
In Madrid, sources at BCH said earlier that the bank had reached an initial agreement to buy 26 to 36 percent of Banco de Colombia in a deal worth $200 million to $260 million.

The statement from Banco de Colombia did not specify how big a stake in bank would be sold to BCH. But it said BCH would become a "signficant" shareholder and participate in the day-to-day management of Banco de Colombia.
To facilitate the purchase, the statement said Banco de Colombia would increase its share capital by 1.2 times book value in the first quarter of 1997.

Banco de Colombia, Colombia's second largest bank in terms of assets, was privatized in 1994 and has total assets of about $3 billion. Grupo Gilinski, the bank's leading shareholders, is one of Colombia's largest industrial and financial conglomerates.

The alliance with BCH should put Banco de Colombia on a better footing to compete with Banco Ganadero, Colombia's largest commerical bank. Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya bought a 40 percent stake in Ganadero's voting stock in August. As part of the deal, Bilbao Vizcaya injected $208 million in fresh equity into the bank, which was already one of the most solvent in Colombia.
